jobs.title: General Manager
jobs.location: Middlefield, Ohio, United States of America
jobs.description:
General Manager
Mercury Plastics has been providing innovative thermoplastic solutions to a variety of markets including; appliance, automotive, construction, liquid dispensing, marine, medical, off-shore oil and plumbing since 1965. We are recognized as an industry leader in our ability to provide unique approaches to profile extrusion, injection overmolding and fabrication of thermoplastic parts.

Mercury Plastics provides PFAS-free manufacturing processes in extrusions and molded components. We are one of only a few companies in North America that has captive electron beam processing; including a 5 MeV electron beam accelerator, which has been in operation since 1999, and a recently added 10 MeV electron beam accelerator. At Mercury, we continually strive to deliver innovative solutions for our customers and a positive impact of sustainability for our environment and our community.

Mercury Plastics is a division of Masco Corporation. Masco is a global leader in the design, manufacture and distribution of branded home improvement and building products.

What you will do
As part of the Mercury Plastics Executive Leadership Team, the General Manager (GM) will work closely with the executive team to develop and implement business plans and strategies to ensure corporate objectives for the product categories are achieved. Key responsibilities include leading the entire strategy and operations for the business unit, P&L management, business development and developing multi-year strategic and financial plans for the business.

How you will do it
Operational & Strategic Leadership
- Lead the development and execution of strategic business plans. Establish performance metrics and drive organizational alignment across all functions. The GM will also oversee Operations (manufacturing, engineering, supply chain & quality) where they play a key role in optimizing process efficiencies and continuous improvement efforts. Additionally, this leader will have P&L accountability and financial oversight of budgets, forecasts and financial reporting.

Customer & Market Focus
- Maintain strong relationships with key customers and develop new business opportunities for expanding custom products & solutions. There will be a major focus on expanding market share and growing revenue for the Electron Beam Processing business while continuing to maintain the core product portfolio.

Team & Culture
- Promote a culture of innovation, operational excellence, continuous improvement and employee engagement. As GM, you will lead cross-functional teams and mentor and coach other leaders to achieve both professional development and organizational goals.

What we look for
- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business or related field
- 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in an engineering or manufacturing environment
- Proven track record of managing P&L and driving operational excellence
- Strong understanding of lean manufacturing, continuous improvement and supply chain management
- Experience with sales and marketing strategy to drive profitable growth, expand market share, and identify new business opportunities
- Excellent team leadership, communication and organizational skills
- Organizational skills

Company: Mercury Plastics

Full time

jobs.description:
WE ARE HIRING! Program Manager (Hybrid – St. Thomas, ON Office) – 12-18 Month Contract

Build your future with Masco Canada!

At Masco Canada, we’re passionate about delivering innovative solutions and exceptional customer experiences. We’re looking for a Program Manager to join our Product & Innovation team. If you thrive in a dynamic, collaborative environment and are excited to make a meaningful impact, we want to hear from you.  This is for a 12–18-month contract.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?
The Program Manager will play a critical role in driving program governance, tracking progress, mitigating risks, and delivering measurable outcomes. Acting as the central point of coordination, this role is responsible for ensuring that projects within each program are executed cohesively and effectively, while promoting collaboration and accountability across all levels of the organization.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES?
- Lead the end-to-end management of programs, including planning, execution, monitoring, and close-out.

- Define program objectives, scope, deliverables, and resource plans in collaboration with business stakeholders.

- Oversee interdependent projects, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and budget requirements.

- Facilitate effective communication among cross-functional teams and executive sponsors.

- Identify and mitigate risks, resolve issues, and adjust plans proactively to maintain progress and alignment.

- Track program performance using established KPIs, providing regular status updates and insights to leadership.

- Support implementation of best practices and continuous improvement in program delivery methodologies.

- Champion cross-functional collaboration to drive accountability and successful program outcomes

WHAT WILL YOU BRING?
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or a related field.

- PMP (Project Management Professional) or equivalent certification is strongly preferred.

- Additional training or certification in Agile, Lean, or Program Management is an asset.

- 5+ years of project or program management experience, preferably within manufacturing, consumer goods, or industrial products.

- Proven ability to manage complex, cross-functional initiatives with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.

- Strong knowledge of project management tools and methodologies, including Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid models.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and influence across all organizational levels.

- Analytical thinker with a focus on problem-solving, risk mitigation, and data-informed decision-making.

- Highly organized and adaptable, with a track record of meeting deadlines and delivering high-impact results.

- Experience in a matrixed environment and in managing change across functions is preferred.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?
- Competitive Rewards and Compensation

- Benefit insurance coverage from Day 1, including health, dental, and travel insurance

- Employee Assistance Program (Dialogue) – access to health and wellness resources

- Employee Store, Employee Purchase Program, Fitness Discounts, and more!

- Opportunities for development and growth, including Buddy and Mentoring programs, LinkedIn Learning, and other virtual and in-class learning opportunities

- Innovative Solutions – Our commitment to  cutting-edge plumbing and water technologies  keeps us at the forefront of the industry.

- Collaborative & Inclusive Culture  – We foster an environment where all employees are  valued, respected, and empowered  to contribute and grow.

jobs.title: Commercial Finance Manager - GTN
jobs.description:
WE ARE HIRING! COMMERCIAL FINANCE MANAGER – GROSS-TO-NET (Onsite - St. Thomas, ON Office)
Build your future with Masco Canada!
At Masco Canada, we’re passionate about delivering innovative solutions and exceptional customer experiences. We’re looking for Commercial Finance Manager – Gross-To-Net, to join our Finance team. If you thrive in a dynamic, collaborative environment and are excited to make a meaningful impact, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
The Commercial Finance Manager (Gross-to-Net) is responsible for the end-to-end management and analysis of Gross-to-Net (GTN), which captures the financial impact of trade programs such as discounts, rebates, chargebacks, promotions, and product returns and represents the difference between gross sales and realized net revenue. This role ensures accurate revenue recognition, provides clear visibility into commercial profitability, and delivers actionable insights to support strategic and operational decision-making. The position requires strong analytical capability, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to effectively partner with Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Finance to optimize trade spend and overall commercial performance.

GROSS-TO-NET MANAGEMENT
- Own the end-to-end GTN process, covering trade discounts, rebates, chargebacks, promotional spend, and returns including:
- Maintain a detailed database of customer agreements and commercial terms; evaluate their impact on net revenue and profitability.

- Monitor GTN performance versus budget/forecast and deliver clear variance analysis with actionable recommendations.

- Oversee accruals and ensure accurate and timely month-end closing of GTN-related items.

- Collaborate with FP&A to develop forward-looking models that forecast GTN impacts by customer, product, and channel.

STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT & BUSINESS PARTNERING
- Act as a trusted finance partner for Sales and Marketing.

- Support promotions, and customer negotiations with robust financial analysis.

- Present complex financial information in simple, business-oriented terms to non-financial stakeholders.

- Build strong cross-functional relationships, balancing commercial objectives with financial governance.

FINANCIAL REPORTING & STRATEGIC ANALYSIS
- Build GTN dashboards and establish KPIs for reporting to leadership.

- Contribute to budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning with a focus on net revenue.

- Perform scenario analysis and ad-hoc financial modeling to support executive decision-making.

- Identify risks and opportunities in GTN and recommend proactive actions.

CONTROLS, GOVERNANCE & COMPLIANCE
- Ensure GTN processes comply with Masco Canada’s policies, internal controls, and audit requirements.

- Partner with Internal Audit and Controllership to strengthen governance related to customer programs and promotions.

- Drive continuous improvement to increase efficiency, accuracy, and transparency in GTN reporting.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related discipline (CPA designation preferred).

- 5+ years of progressive finance experience, ideally in manufacturing, distribution, or consumer goods.

- Expertise in revenue management, trade spend, or Gross-to-Net processes.

- Strong financial modeling, variance analysis, and forecasting capabilities.

- Advanced Excel and ERP system proficiency (JD Edwards, SAP, Oracle, or equivalent).

- Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage complex datasets accurately.

- Strong business acumen with the ability to translate financial insights into business recommendations.

- Proven ability to influence, challenge, and build consensus with diverse stakeholders.

- Organized, proactive, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?
- Competitive Rewards and Compensation

- Defined Contribution Registered Pension Plan (optional) with employer matching

- Deferred Profit-Sharing Plan (DPSP)

- Benefit insurance coverage from Day 1, including health, dental, and travel insurance

- Employee Assistance Program (Dialogue) – access to health and wellness resources

- Employee Store, Employee Purchase Program, Dell Discount Program, GoodLife Fitness Discounts, and more

- 2 paid volunteer days to support the communities we live and work in

- Opportunities for development and growth, including Onboarding, Buddy and Mentoring programs, LinkedIn Learning, and other virtual and in-class learning opportunities

- Participation in employee-led committees such as the Wellness Committee, Masco United (Inclusion & Belonging Committee), Philanthropy Committee, Organizational Pulse Committee, or employee impact groups

WHY JOIN MASCO CANADA?
- Over a Century of Excellence  – With more than  120+ years of experience , Masco Canada has established itself as a leader in the  building and home improvement industry .
- Diverse Brand Portfolio  – We proudly offer  12+ brands  delivering  20,000+ innovative water solutions , shaping the future of plumbing and home improvement.
- Innovative Solutions – Our commitment to  cutting-edge plumbing and water technologies  keeps us at the forefront of the industry.
- Collaborative & Inclusive Culture  – We foster an environment where all employees are  valued, respected, and empowered  to contribute and grow.
- Opportunities for Growth  – We support  continuous learning, career development, and professional growth , helping you achieve your full potential.
- Making an Impact in Our Communities  – We believe in  giving back  and actively supporting initiatives that  make a difference in the communities where we live and work .

Join us at Masco Canada , where your contributions drive  innovation, excellence, and positive change !

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager – Enterprise Commercial Performance Management
jobs.location: Livonia, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Masco is hiring a   Senior Program Manager of Enterprise Commercial Performance Management   to strengthen and scale its enterprise approach to commercial performance. This role enables leadership to   operate   from a clear, consistent, and market-informed view of performance and improves decision-making and accountability across business units.

Key Responsibilities

Own and Evolve the Commercial Performance Framework
This role   is responsible   for   shaping and governing Masco’s enterprise commercial performance framework, bringing clarity to how performance is defined, measured, and reviewed across the business. It   establishes   a focused set of KPIs, ensures data is clearly defined and owned, and continuously simplifies the approach so leaders can rely on a clear, decision-ready view of performance.

Enable Enterprise Adoption and Compliance
This role partners with business units to implement the performance framework in ways that align with   enterprise standards while reflecting each BU’s strategies and operating realities. It drives adoption through clear communication, practical enablement, and consistent business rhythms, while working closely with IT, Business Intelligence, Finance, and Commercial teams to   establish   efficient, scalable reporting processes.

Deliver   Decision ‑ Enabling   Performance Visibility
The role ensures leaders have a consistent and actionable view of performance, grounded in standardized dashboards designed to support   decision-making. Rather than reactive reporting, it builds a repeatable, fact-based approach that connects topline performance, mix, and growth dynamics to underlying business drivers.

Lead Market Growth Intelligence and Insights
A critical   component   of the role is connecting internal performance with external market reality. By integrating market data from business units into a consistent, enterprise perspective, the role builds a coherent enterprise view of growth and share, ensuring market insights are   a core part of performance discussions and strategic decisions.

Build and Lead the Commercial Performance Team
The role also builds and leads the team responsible for performance reporting, analytics, and market intelligence. This includes setting priorities,   establishing   quality standards, and building a scalable capability.

Qualifications

- 8-9 years of experience in commercial finance, performance management, business intelligence, or enterprise analytics roles.

- Strong commercial and financial acumen,   with a deep understanding of topline performance, mix, and market dynamics.

- Demonstrated experience designing standardized, scalable measurement and reporting processes that enable   decision ‑ making .

- Experience leading small teams within complex, matrixed,   multi ‑ business   organizations with enterprise stakeholders.

- Ability to lead teams to build market growth and outlook estimates from multiple data sources, with the ability to scale toward more advanced analytical rigor.

- Proven ability to influence without   authority and partner effectively with senior commercial and finance leaders.

- Early ‑ career   experience in a structured finance or analytics development program strongly preferred.

What Success Looks Like

- An   enterprise ‑ wide   commercial performance KPI framework is   established , with clear definitions, ownership, and a consistent operating cadence.

- Leadership   operates   from a clear, consistent, and trusted view of commercial performance across the enterprise.

- Business units   broadly adopt   the framework and use it   as the primary lens for performance review and accountability.

- The KPI set is simplified and focused, with redundant or   non ‑ value ‑ added   measures or ad hoc analysis eliminated.

- Each BU has a tailored, trusted approach to market estimation integrated into a consistent enterprise-wide view of market growth and outlook.

- Standardized dashboards and reporting materially reduce the time spent by Masco HQ and business units creating performance reports.

jobs.title: Operations Finance Manager
jobs.location: Lapeer, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
At Delta Faucet , we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence.

Your Role at Delta Faucet:
The Plant Accounting Manager will support plant operations management financially by maintaining the general ledger, handling month-end close, forecasting and budgeting, controlling inventory, and preparing weekly, monthly, and annual reports for management. This role is essential in delivering insights to plant leadership that drive cost reduction, operational excellence, and strategic decisions.
Reporting directly to the Category Controller, this role partners with Finance teams at headquarters, plant leadership, and other Masco locations. The Plant Accounting Manager’s success is reflected in cost per earned hour oversight, cycle count reliability, and preventing SOX control deficiencies.

Responsibilities:
- Direct the implementation of all accounting policies and procedures to guarantee complete adherence to Sarbanes-Oxley regulations.
- Manage the month-end close process, including financial reporting and variance analysis.
- Manage budgeting, forecasting, and reporting for labor, overhead, scrap, and capital by implementing actionable variance analysis.
- Collaborate with operations to offer financial assistance for ongoing improvement efforts.
- Monitor and analyze overhead spending, labor efficiency, and cost drivers to identify potential issues and savings opportunities.
- Deliver timely, clear, and insightful financial reports to plant management and headquarters.
- Coordinate cycle-count and inventory control programs, including reconciliations and compliance with corporate standards.
- Contribute and support strategic projects and initiatives.

Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in accounting (CMA/CPA preferred) with 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing environment (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Access, Word); experience with SAP ERP systems preferred.

jobs.title: Manager, FP&A Sales & Margins
jobs.location: Vista, California, United States of America
jobs.description:
Watkins Wellness is hiring a Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis – Product Sales & Margins to join our Finance team!

DISCOVER
In this highly visible role, you'll help shape financial decision-making across the business by leading forecasting, budgeting, reporting, and analysis for sales, cost of sales, and margin performance. You'll partner closely with business leaders, provide insights into key business drivers, and help find opportunities and risks that influence company results.
Leading a team of three Senior Analysts, you'll play an important role in developing talent, improving processes, and creating a high-performing FP&A function. This position supports a General Manager business segment and requires someone who can quickly learn complex processes, leverage financial systems and analytics tools, and drive continuous improvement in a fast-paced environment. You'll balance critical thinking with hands-on execution while presenting insights and recommendations to leadership and executive collaborators.

YOUR RIPPLE EFFECT
- Do you enjoy leading and developing high-performing teams? Manage and mentor a team of FP&A analysts by providing direction, coaching, performance feedback, and leadership that supports individual and team success.
- Can you turn financial data into meaningful business decisions? Lead forecasting, budgeting, long-range planning, documentation, and examination activities for revenue, cost of goods sold, and profitability outcomes while identifying key trends, opportunities, and risks.
- Do you thrive when building strong partnerships across the business? Serve as a trusted finance partner to business leaders, supporting a business segment with actionable financial insights and guidance that improve decision-making.
- Are you energized by continuous improvement and process optimization? Drive enhancements to planning processes, financial models, reporting tools, and systems that improve efficiency, accuracy, and business visibility.
- Can you manage complex planning cycles and competing priorities? Coordinate key portions of the forecast, budget, and long-range planning processes while ensuring high-quality deliverables and adherence to reporting deadlines.
- Do you enjoy leveraging technology and analytics to solve business challenges? Create, enhance, and maintain reports and financial models using tools such as Excel, Workday Adaptive Planning, SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), Hyperion/SmartView, and other enterprise systems.
- Are you comfortable presenting financial insights to senior leaders? Translate complex financial information into clear, actionable recommendations and communicate findings effectively to management and executive stakeholders.
- Can you operate effectively in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity? Take ownership of projects and business initiatives, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and execute with urgency while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

WHAT YOU BRING
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
- 7+ years of experience in an FP&A or Senior Financial Analyst role.
- Prior experience leading people, projects, or cross-functional initiatives.
- Strong budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and analytical capabilities.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills required.
- Experience with financial planning and reporting systems such as Workday Adaptive Planning, SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), Hyperion/SmartView, or similar enterprise planning solutions.
- ERP system experience, such as Navision, Oracle, SAP, or comparable platforms.
- Strong organizational, communication, presentation, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to build effective teams, work collaboratively, and influence stakeholders at multiple levels of the organization.
- Experience with Power BI is a plus.
- CPA and/or advanced degree preferred but not required.

WHAT YOU’LL GET
At Watkins Wellness, we believe that everyone should ‘Feel good. Live well’. We offer employees the opportunity to join a dynamic, growing industry leader with an outstanding and well-deserved reputation for leadership and commitment to our employees, customers and community. Our employees are eligible to receive exceptional health and wellness benefits, paid time off, company bonus, profit sharing, 401k match, education assistance, and much more. We are proud of the people we are and the products we make — products that make a difference to the health and well-being of others.

We look for candidates that exhibit The Watkins Way (always Ethical, endeavors to be Transparent, embraces Inclusion, welcomes Diverse backgrounds and perspectives, Accommodating, believes in Work-Life Balance, puts Safety First, Accountable, values Relationships, Passionate, Team Player, and Goal Driven).

The employee must frequently lift and move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision and depth perception. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.
